title: "Import as: Mesh Library" from gltf/glb does not import collision and navigation meshes via node suffixes
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.7.1, 4.8-dev4 ### System information Godot v4.7.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1656) - AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor (8 threads) - 61.55 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description In the import settings of GLTF and GLB files, you can specify via a dropdown to import the file as either a scene or a mesh library and a couple other things. When you select the Mesh Library option: It is able to successfully import the file as a MeshLibrary resource, except for the fact that it does not appear to support importing any custom collision or navigation meshes. It will show them in the scene view of the full import dialog - for example, here in the reproducing project, you can see in the scene tab it has detected the "cube-colonly" and "cube-navmesh" nodes in the original file and created collision mesh and navigation mesh nodes in the import dialog: However, if you look at the Mesh Library editor view tab on the bottom (after assigning the .glb file to a GridMap node), you will see that it does not show any collision or navigation meshes: However, if you use the traditional Mesh Library import workflow: importing the the .glb/.gltf file as a Scene, create a new inherited scene from it, exporting the scene as a Mesh Library, then assigning it to a GridMap node, you'll notice that the collision and navigation meshes (via the node name suffixes) are imported and configured correctly into the MeshLibrary resource you export. I would expect the "Import as: Mesh Library" workflow should behave the same as the traditional workflow, except streamlining the inherited scene/export as meshlibrary steps. ### Steps to reproduce - Create a blank Godot project, with an empty "models" folder - Create a blank scene, e.g. main.tscn, and add a GridMap node - Create a simple blender project - Add at least one mesh node in the project (it can just be a cube) - Add any combination of nodes with the special suffixes, like *-colonly, *-navmesh, or just naming the mesh *-col - Export the blender project as a .glb file in the models folder of the godot project - materials don't matter - Select the .glb file in the Godot project, and in the Import As: dropdown, select Mesh Library - Select the GridMap node and drag the .glb file to the Mesh Library property - Open the Mesh Library editor tab on the bottom - Notice that collision and navigation meshes are not assigned in the Mesh Library ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [tilemap-import-bug-test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31987466/tilemap-import-bug-test.zip)
